candidates.attacker_control: Both `callerUrl` and `redirectUrl` are plain HTTP request parameters. ControlledVocabularyServlet is reachable anonymously by GET or POST; SearchResultLogServlet is reachable anonymously by POST (its `query` parameter must be supplied to avoid a NullPointerException in Arrays.asList(request.getParameterValues("query")) before the redirect line). Values such as `http://evil.example/`, `//evil.example/` or `https://evil.example/` flow unmodified into sendRedirect().
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked that neither servlet is under the admin-only or registered-only filter mappings (web.xml lines 74-117), so anonymous reachability holds. Checked that neither servlet nor any JSPUI filter performs same-origin validation of these parameters (searched all sendRedirect uses in dspace-jspui; other servlets build targets from request.getContextPath() or server-side handles, while these two pass raw parameters). Confirmed that response.encodeRedirectURL() is absent in these two calls and, even where present elsewhere, does not validate external targets. Confirmed the POST-only entry point for /dso-display and the need for a non-null `query` value to reach line 71. Verified the mapping names/classes in web.xml match the servlets. Source-only analysis; no runtime confirmation.
candidates.impact: An unauthenticated attacker can craft a URL on the trusted DSpace host that redirects the victim to an arbitrary external site. This enables phishing/credential-harvesting campaigns that abuse the repository's reputation and origin (e.g., fake login pages reached from a legitimate-looking DSpace link), and can be combined with OAuth/SSO or referrer-based trust flows. The /dso-display servlet also logs a usage event before redirecting, so the redirect appears as legitimate search-result traffic.
candidates.prerequisites: The DSpace JSPUI webapp is deployed and the two servlets are mapped (web.xml lines 757-759 map controlledvocabulary to /controlledvocabulary; lines 781-784 map SearchResultLogServlet to /dso-display). No authentication or role is required: the admin-only filter covers only /dspace-admin/* and registered-only covers /tools/*, /submit, /profile, /subscribe, /workspace, /view-workspaceitem, /mydspace only (web.xml lines 79-117), so neither /controlledvocabulary nor /dso-display is behind a filter. The victim must follow an attacker-supplied link/form (for /dso-display the request is a POST, e.g., an auto-submitted form on an attacker page).
candidates.root_cause: Request parameters are used directly as HTTP redirect targets without any validation that they resolve to the local application. ControlledVocabularyServlet.doDSGet() reads `callerUrl` (line 38) and calls response.sendRedirect(callerUrl) (line 53); doDSPost() delegates to doDSGet(). SearchResultLogServlet.doDSPost() reads `redirectUrl` (line 40) and calls response.sendRedirect(redirectUrl) (line 71). Neither servlet prefixes the context path, checks for a leading '/' vs a scheme/'//', nor restricts the host; encodeRedirectURL() (used elsewhere in the codebase but not here for the target) only rewrites session IDs and performs no target validation.
candidates.title: Open redirect via unvalidated redirect targets in JSPUI (ControlledVocabularyServlet and SearchResultLogServlet)
candidates.trace: 1) web.xml maps `controlledvocabulary` to /controlledvocabulary and `SearchResultLogServlet` to /dso-display with no auth filter. 2) GET /controlledvocabulary?callerUrl=http://evil.example/ -> ControlledVocabularyServlet.doDSGet reads callerUrl (line 38, stored in session for UI purposes at lines 50-52) and calls response.sendRedirect(callerUrl) (line 53) -> 302 Location: http://evil.example/. 3) POST /dso-display with params query=x&redirectUrl=http://evil.example/ -> doDSPost reads redirectUrl (line 40); HandleManager.resolveToObject()/substringAfter() only derive logging values and do not constrain the target; the search event is fired (lines 47-68) and response.sendRedirect(redirectUrl) (line 71) issues the external 302.
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-confirmed and not verified against upstream fix history: it is possible these endpoints are considered legacy/unused in some deployments, that a front proxy rewrites or blocks external Location headers, or that the snapshots' ground-truth issue is a different weakness. The open-redirect behavior itself follows directly from the source lines cited.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-601 URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

coverage_summary: Source scope: 2,028 files visible (binary-like files refused; no other exclusions, 0 symlinks/sensitive-name exclusions). The P1 relation index is partial: 1,780 files indexed, 1,464 parsed Java files, 248 source files missing from the index (JSP/XSL/config/static and other non-Java files), no control-flow or data-flow analysis and no semantic resolution; no index facts beyond name-based security_call hints were available, and those hints were verified against source text. I inspected: dspace-jspui servlets (including controlled vocabulary, search result log, handle, admin, profile/registration/password), filters and web.xml filter/servlet mappings; JSPs under controlledvocabulary, search, suggest, feedback, dspace-admin, tools; dspace-api authorization helpers (AuthorizeManager/AuthorizeUtil), authentication methods, AccountManager, browse DAOs/engine, controlled-vocabulary authority and XPath use, ItemImport, license/CreativeCommons, packager/METS, media filter execs; dspace-rest resources; dspace-oai data/filter layer; sample SWORDv2 zip ingester; LNI DAVResource. Not exhaustively reviewed: XMLUI aspect/aspect transformers and XSLs, full dspace-sword/s v2 stacks, statistics/Elasticsearch reporting, Solr configuration, JSP static assets, and most configuration/build files. No code was executed and no external services were queried.
limitations: The relation index omits 248 non-Java files (including JSP/XSL/config), so JSP-only weaknesses (e.g., the raw reflections in controlledvocabulary.jsp, eperson-browse.jsp, creative-commons-edit.jsp) could not be checked for patch/removal traces; no unreported area should be assumed reviewed.
The index has no data-flow or reachability proof; all traces in this report were re-verified by reading the cited source lines.

The snapshot version metadata (poms say 4.4) is inconsistent with the code generation (Bootstrap/jQuery-era JSPUI, Spring addon services), so the exact upstream release and the corresponding security-fix history could not be established from the snapshot alone; no patch, CVE, or upstream comparison data was inspected per the review rules.
No deployment configuration (proxy rules, enabled webapps) is present, so real-world reachability of the JSPUI and /dso-display depends on deployment choices.
No runtime confirmation, tests, or scanners were run; candidate status is a lead, not a confirmed vulnerability.

rejected_leads.lead: Zip Slip / path traversal in ItemImport ZIP extraction: `new FileOutputStream(ziptempdir + entry.getName())` (dspace-api/src/main/java/org/dspace/app/itemimport/ItemImport.java lines 526, 542, 552) writes entries without checking for `..` or absolute names.
rejected_leads.reason: Real unsafe pattern, but the extraction code path is only reached from the `dspace import` command-line entry point (main/runImport). The only web caller of ItemImport (BatchMetadataImportServlet -> processUploadableImport) handles BTE metadata files, not the ZIP archive branch. No web-reachable caller found, so external attacker impact is not established; treated as a hardening/local-admin lead, not the top candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: Reflected XSS in publicly reachable JSPs: dspace-jspui/src/main/webapp/controlledvocabulary/controlledvocabulary.jsp inserts session values derived from request parameters (`ID` at line 69 inside a <script> block, `filter` at lines 110/138) without HTML/JS escaping; dspace-admin/eperson-browse.jsp:139 and tools/creative-commons-edit.jsp:62 also echo request parameters unescaped.
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible and potentially higher impact, but attribution is uncertain: these pages are legacy code that may predate the escaped outputs found in feedback/form.jsp, search/advanced.jsp, search/results.jsp and suggest/suggest.jsp, and I could not confirm (without patch/upstream data) that a security fix was removed here. eperson-browse and creative-commons-edit additionally require admin/registered sessions. Kept as an unconfirmed lead rather than the single candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: SSRF via CreativeCommons.fetchURL/fetchLicenseRDF (dspace-api/src/main/java/org/dspace/license/CreativeCommons.java lines 314-321, 427-450) reached from EditItemServlet.showEditForm with request parameter `cc_license_url` (dspace-jspui/.../admin/EditItemServlet.java lines 406-416), which lets the server fetch an arbitrary URL.
rejected_leads.reason: Reachability requires `AuthorizeUtil.authorizeManageCCLicense` (item ADD+REMOVE rights, item/collection/community admin, or system admin), so an unauthenticated user cannot trigger it; impact is limited to privileged users causing outbound requests. Not selected.

rejected_leads.lead: Potential XXE in the optional LNI module: DAVResource parses attacker-supplied XML with plain `new SAXBuilder()` (dspace-lni/src/main/java/org/dspace/app/dav/DAVResource.java lines 607, 860, 1209, 1678, 1770) and SimpleHTMLFragment parses XML with SAXBuilder in XMLUI.
rejected_leads.reason: JDOM 1.x default entity behavior was not verifiable from this snapshot's sources, the LNI webapp is a separate optional deployment, and no confirming data flow from an untrusted remote endpoint to a dangerous entity sink was traced. Unconfirmed, not submitted.

rejected_leads.lead: OAI-PMH database repository builds SQL by concatenating filter fragments (dspace-oai/.../DSpaceItemDatabaseRepository.java lines 183-187, 237-241).
rejected_leads.reason: Traced the filter implementations (DSpaceAtLeastOneMetadataFilter, DspaceSetSpecFilter, date filters): values are bound with `?` parameters and the concatenated fragments are static strings/IDs, so no injection was demonstrated. Also, the Solr repository is normally used first. Rejected as unconfirmed.

summary: This is a DSpace (Java, multi-webapp: dspace-api, dspace-jspui, dspace-xmlui, dspace-rest, dspace-oai, sword/swordv2, lni) snapshot. I reviewed the Java source broadly (JSPUI servlets/filters/JSPs, REST resources, OAI data layer, SWORDv2 ingesters, core authorization helpers, ItemImport/packager code) and traced attacker-controlled request parameters into security-sensitive sinks. The strongest concrete issue is an unvalidated redirect (CWE-601): two anonymous JSPUI endpoints pass a raw request parameter to HttpServletResponse.sendRedirect() with no same-origin validation, allowing an attacker to redirect victims to an arbitrary external site from the trusted repository origin. I also examined several plausible but weaker/reachability-limited leads (Zip Slip in the CLI ItemImport ZIP extraction, raw JSP reflections, SSRF in CreativeCommons license fetch, XXE candidates in optional modules) and did not find evidence elevating them above the open redirect. No runtime testing was performed; all conclusions are source-level.
